name: Pochoir
summary: Colour put on by hand through a set of cut stencils, one for each colour, over a printed key line.
how: Cut one stencil from zinc, copper or celluloid for each colour of the original; a plate can need 20–100 stencils.
Put on gouache or watercolour with a round brush (pompon) in a dabbing motion, so the edge stays clean.
Align each stencil by eye to the printed key line.
Mix each colour to match the original and keep it flat and opaque.

origin.note: Paul Iribe's album Les Robes de Paul Poiret is coloured by hand through stencils, and Paris fashion takes up the method. This is a landmark, not the first use: André Marty and Jean Saudé ran stencil studios in the 1890s.

adoptions.via: Lucien Vogel launches the Gazette du Bon Ton, with plates by Barbier, Lepape and Martin coloured in pochoir.
Artists of ROSTA paint news strips through paper stencils, one stencil for each colour, for the shop windows of Moscow.
